qualification: Seats are positions authorized, filled or vacant: 677 district positions (48 vacant), 345 bankruptcy judgeships authorized and funded (63 vacant), and 593 magistrate judge positions (567 full time, 24 part time, 2 combined with a clerk’s post), all as of September 30, 2025. The courts’ 677 district positions are the 673 judgeships of 28 U.S.C. 133’s table and the 4 of the three territorial district courts (Guam 1, the Northern Mariana Islands 1, the Virgin Islands 2), which Title 48 sets and whose judges serve ten-year terms, not for life; the Administrative Office’s table of authorized district judgeships agrees court by court. No temporary district judgeship remains: Pub. L. 118-203 of December 23, 2024 made the last ten permanent, and the courts counted 677 in every year from 2021 to 2025. The statute table lists 316 bankruptcy judgeships; the 29 more the courts count were not traced. No appointing president or party is recorded.

notes: Statute tables summed by script: 28 U.S.C. 133(a) lists 673 district judgeships, four of them shared between districts; 152(a)(2) lists 316 bankruptcy judgeships, and its notes carry temporary judgeships

Traced November 13, 2026 (ledger claim 28): 677 = 673 + 4. The Administrative Office’s "Additional Authorized Judgeships" table (January 2025) lists 104 district rows summing to 677; its 97 rows with seats equal, court by court, the 94 statute rows and 3 territorial rows of uscode-federal-courts-circuits-districts. Its "Authorized Temporary Judgeships" list shows the last ten temporary district judgeships (Alabama Northern, Arizona, California Central, Florida Southern, Hawaii, Kansas, Missouri Eastern, New Mexico, North Carolina Western, Texas Eastern) made permanent by Pub. L. 118-203, December 23, 2024. Judicial Business 2025, Table 10, gives 677 district positions for 2021 to 2025.

U.S. Code currency, checked November 13, 2026: each section this file draws reads the same, word for word with spaces set aside, in the Office of the Law Revision Counsel’s release current through Public Law 119-138 (November 3, 2026) as in the 2024 edition govinfo serves; Public Laws 119-139 to 119-142, which Congress.gov lists after it, amend none of them (28 U.S.C. 133, 134, 152, 631 and 633).
